run.notes: Short-prompt/long-generation concurrency (128 in / 512 out), the shape CLAUDE.md flagged as untested after the 2026-09-03 512/128 sweep. Primary numbers are from a thermally-controlled pass (card cooled to 52C before every level, cooled.json); the uncontrolled ascending pass is concurrency.json. ONLY c=1 AND c=16 REPRODUCE. c=2/4/8 are bimodal, the variance is entirely in TPOT with TTFT constant, and the thermal explanation was tested and rejected (c=16 is hottest, fastest and most stable; fast and slow trials occur at equal temperature and clock; minima reproduce to 0.2% across passes). Every generation hit the 512-token cap, so this measures the reasoning phase: throughput real, task fictional.

hardware.accelerator: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti with Max-Q Design

host.notes: TU117, compute capability 7.5, NO tensor cores. Max-Q: thermally throttled, and it inverted a curve once.

model.architecture_notes: Reasoning model: tokens arrive as reasoning_content until the thinking block closes. Every cell here ran to the 512-token cap with finish_reason length.

workload.tool: sweep.py (copy of gpu-pytorch-g5g-2b, three bugs fixed)
workload.notes: decode-source auto -> stream; llama-server emits no usage.decode_tokens_per_second. Prompt cache VERIFIED defeated: llamacpp:prompt_tokens_cached_total 0 against prompt_tokens_total 17689.

issues.summary: Decode batching is intermittent below c=16: at c=2 the slow mode's TPOT is 29.6 ms/token, exactly 2x the c=1 figure of 14.4, i.e. streams taking turns rather than batching. Cause unknown; arrival timing against llama.cpp batch formation is the untested suspect.
--repeats 3 cannot characterise a bimodal cell. The 2026-09-03 repeats fix assumed noise around a single value; a median of two modes is worse than reporting both.
c=8 measured 160.5 and 159.8 early in the session and ~110-128 later, with no configuration change. Not reproducible.

NOT A DEFECT - closed investigation. Thermal throttling investigated as the cause of the spreads and REJECTED on three independent grounds. Heat is real (clocks fall ~10% within a level, power capped at ~39W of 40W) but is not what these spreads are.

notes: SHORT-PROMPT / LONG-GENERATION DOES SCALE, unlike the long-prompt shape: 63.8 -> 164.1 tok/s, 2.6x from c=1, against 1.47x for 512/128 on 2026-09-03. Prefill does not batch and is the minority of the work at this shape, which is exactly why it pays here.
c=16 is the only multi-stream level that reproduced across every pass (0.2% spread, 164.0/164.1/164.4). It is the only high-concurrency number from this rig worth quoting.
The curve appears to FALL from c=1 to c=2 (63.77 -> 62.58). That is an artifact of median selection over two modes, not a result.
Per-stream throughput at c=16 is 10.3 tok/s. Peak aggregate and usable interactive latency remain far apart on this card.
